source: GDOS (Generalna Dyrekcja Ochrony Srodowiska / General Directorate for Environmental Protection), Centralny Rejestr Form Ochrony Przyrody (CRFOP), layer PomnikiPrzyrodyPunktowe (point-geometry natural monuments), filtered to obiekt='drzewo' (tree)
endpoint: https://sdi.gdos.gov.pl/wfs (WFS 2.0.0, typeName=GDOS:PomnikiPrzyrodyPunktowe, srsName=EPSG:4326 requested and served correctly reprojected, axis order lon,lat)
licence_proof: dane.gov.pl (Poland's official national open-data portal, run under the Polish Act on the re-use of public sector information) dataset record id 471 'Centralny Rejestr Form Ochrony Przyrody', institution 'Generalna Dyrekcja Ochrony Srodowiska' (the same body that operates the sdi.gdos.gov.pl WFS): API field license_name = "CC0 1.0", license_description = "Other (Public Domain)" (fetched 2026-08-15 via https://api.dane.gov.pl/1.4/datasets/471,centralny-rejestr-form-ochrony-przyrody). This resolves the contradiction the 2026-07-30 scan flagged: the WFS GetCapabilities carries no licence text at all (ows:Fees and ows:AccessConstraints both literally 'brak', i.e. blank, re-verified live 2026-08-15), and gov.pl's page-footer statement of CC BY-SA 4.0 (also re-verified, present on www.gov.pl/web/gdos) is generic gov.pl PLATFORM boilerplate ('Tresci tekstowe publikowane w serwisie...' = text content published on the site, i.e. articles and pages), NOT a dataset-specific licence and not about structured open data at all. The dataset-specific CC0 declaration on dane.gov.pl, tied to this exact dataset id and this exact institution, is the primary, authoritative statement and is what this import relies on.
designation: Pomnik przyrody (natural monument), point-geometry natural monuments designated under Poland's Nature Conservation Act (Ustawa o ochronie przyrody), obiekt='drzewo' filter applied to exclude boulders (glaz narzutowy), rock outcrops (skalka), springs (zrodlo), caves and shrubs also carried by the same layer
scope: NOT a national import. The full layer holds 117,474 point natural monuments nationally (the largest verified register pool found anywhere in this project); importing all of it was explicitly out of scope for this pass. This file holds only entries inside a roughly 0.2-degree (~22km) bounding box around five sprint-priority cities: Wroclaw, Poznan, Warsaw, Krakow, Gdansk. 8,053 tree entries fetched across the five boxes with zero gid overlap between cities. Of those, 1,943 carry designation_type='jednoobiektowy' (single-object, i.e. one individually designated tree) and 6,110 carry 'wieloobiektowy' (multi-object: 4,023 'aleja' avenues, 1,966 'grupa drzew' groups of trees, 121 'inny'/unspecified other). Each row is ONE POINT PER LEGAL DESIGNATION, not one point per member tree: unlike the Czech AOPK layer, an avenue of 100 trees here is a single row with a single representative coordinate, so no member-tree explosion happened and none of the wieloobiektowy rows needed to be dropped the way Czech's were. The collectible-point test (is this avenue/group actually one thing to stand at, or should it stay a lead) is still a city-pass judgement, exactly as it is for Portugal's Alameda and Conjunto arboreo entries.
caveat: Three things a run must know before using this. (1) This schema is thinner than Portugal, Czech or Italy: GDOS's point layer carries no girth, height, crown or age field at all, only species (as a combined Polish-common-name-plus-Latin-binomial string in 'species_pl_latin'), an optional proper name, the legal designation date, and a link to the CRFOP web record for that entry (crfop.gdos.gov.pl, itself behind an Incapsula bot-check and not fetchable by curl this pass; the WFS is the only machine-readable route). A city pass will need the CRFOP web page or another source for measurements. (2) No vitality field exists in this layer; 'alive now' remains a per-tree check, same as every register scanned so far. (3) 'designated' (data_utwor) is the legal designation date, not a planting or survey date, and predates the tree's actual age by design; some designation dates run back to the 1950s-70s, which is at least weak evidence the tree itself is considerably older still.
